Mint a grounding token for a set of facts

Source: R/grounding.R
grounding_token.Rd

Reduces a vector of verification dates to a single grounding token. A fact is grounded only when its verification date is present, so an empty set and a set containing any missing date both yield GROUNDING_UNVERIFIED.

Usage

grounding_token(verified_on)

Arguments

verified_on

A vector of verification dates, one per fact. Any type for which is.na() is meaningful is accepted; only missingness is inspected, never the date values themselves. A zero-length vector is valid and means "no facts were checked".

Value

A length-1 character vector: GROUNDING_GROUNDED when every element is present, GROUNDING_UNVERIFIED otherwise.

Details

The asymmetry is deliberate and is the whole point of the vocabulary. An empty evidence set is not neutral – it is the absence of evidence – and a partially checked set is not partially trustworthy, because the consumer has no way to tell which element it may lean on. Both collapse to the unverified token so that a downstream gate errs towards abstention.

See also

combine_grounding for combining tokens rather than dates.

Author

Max Moldovan

Examples

grounding_token(as.Date(c("2026-07-05", "2026-07-06")))
#> [1] "grounded"
grounding_token(as.Date(c("2026-07-05", NA)))
#> [1] "ungrounded"
grounding_token(as.Date(character(0)))
#> [1] "ungrounded"
